description: Machine-readable registry of all Pathway design system components. AI agents building products read this to discover available components, their props, and their file locations.

sidenav.description: Persistent vertical navigation panel. Two levels of depth, expanded/collapsed states, responsive (push/overlay/hidden). Optional NavSectionLabel headings + optional SideNavListSection for contextual link lists.

items.description: Flat navigation tree — use this OR `sections`, not both. Each item: { id, label, icon?, children? }

sections.description: Sectioned navigation — renders NavSectionLabel headings between groups (or rail dividers in collapsed mode). Use this OR `items`.

listSection.description: Optional flat contextual list appended after the main nav (e.g. 'Recent Content'). Hidden in collapsed rail.

activeId.description: ID of the currently active navigation item

onNavigate.description: Called when user clicks a destination

scrollbar.description: System-wide overlay scrollbar. Hides the native OS scrollbar and renders one slim semitransparent thumb so scrolling is identical on macOS/Windows/iOS/Android and never takes layout space or shifts padding. Wrap any internal scroll region in <Scrollable>. First consumer: SideNav.

style.description: Wrapper style (positioning context). Use flex:1; minHeight:0 in a flex column.

viewStyle.description: Inner scroll-view style (content flex layout, gap, padding).

viewClassName.description: Extra class on the inner scroll view

checkbox.description: Multi-select selection control. Three states: unchecked, checked, indeterminate. Supports error, highlight, and secondary indeterminate variants. Two sizes. 44×44px touch target always.

indeterminate.description: Shows dash icon; overrides checked visually; sets aria-checked=mixed

error.description: Error / negative styling — fill and border switch to negative token family

highlight.description: Tinted background on the state-layer at rest — for selectable rows

secondary.description: Secondary indeterminate variant (muted colour) — use with indeterminate only

disabled.description: Non-interactive; still accessible to screen readers

size.description: Visual size of the control. Touch target is always 44×44px.

onChange.description: Called on user interaction with the new checked value

className.description: Additional CSS class on the root element

describedBy.description: aria-describedby pointing to an error message element (error state)

gaps: 8 tokens missing from token file — see spec §5.3. fill.action.secondary.* affects highlight variant resting state (HIGH priority).
Secondary Indeterminate use case TBD — confirm with design before shipping.
Highlight variant resting-state token (fill.action.secondary.rest) missing — fallback in use.
checkbox.moduleNote: FIXED 2026-10-02: the checked glyph was bound to foreground-action-primary-ON-SUBTLE-rest while the box is filled with fill-action-primary-strong-*, so the tick was #345499 on #3a5aaa, a 1.12:1 contrast, and the whole square read as a solid blue block with no visible tick. Same bug on the error variant: #722121 on #b03a3a at 1.80:1. Both now use the ON-STRONG foreground, which is #ffffff in BOTH modes: 6.52:1 and 5.98:1 in Light, 5.62:1 and 5.98:1 in Midnight. Figma binds Foreground/Static/Neutral/MONO for the tick, which is correct in Light but wrong in Midnight, because mono is an INVERSION ANCHOR rather than a rung and flips to #181b2b, putting a near-black tick on a blue box at 3.04:1. on-strong is the right token for a foreground on a strong fill. See figmaDefect.
checkbox.figmaDefect: The checked glyph binds Foreground/Static/Neutral/Mono. That is correct in Light (#ffffff) and wrong in Midnight: mono is an inversion anchor, not a rung, so it resolves to #181b2b and puts a near-black tick on a blue box (3.04:1). It should be Foreground/Action/Primary/On Strong, which is #ffffff in both modes. The same applies to the error variants, which should use Foreground/Action/Status/Negative/On Strong. The repo already uses the on-strong tokens.

org-switcher.description: Organisation context switcher trigger in the brand-blue top nav. Renders the active org name (truncated with ellipsis at 180px desktop / 50px mobile). For Catholic organisations only, a second container after the org name shows the city or diocese. The trigger opens a drop panel listing accessible orgs.
org-switcher.v1Scope: Trigger only. Drop panel is a non-normative placeholder in v1 — see spec §0.

orgName.description: Full organisation name. Truncates with ellipsis at 180px desktop / 50px mobile.

orgType.description: Discriminant. Catholic orgs render a second container after the org name (CityName.Catholic). Protestant orgs render the org name on its own (no pipe, no second container).

cityName.description: City or diocese name. RENDERED ONLY when orgType === "catholic" (spec §0.1). Ignored for Protestant orgs even if supplied. NOT a campus/suborg/region name.

logoUrl.description: Org logo URL. Empty or omitted → church SVG placeholder (never text initials).

open.description: Controlled open state — flips the chevron icon 180°.

onClick.description: () => void — fired when the trigger is activated. Caller toggles the open state.

disabled.description: True for single-org users. Trigger renders inert at 50% opacity.

mobile.description: Force the mobile compact display regardless of viewport.

orgs.description: (Panel only — out of scope in v1.) Array of org records for the placeholder panel.

activeOrgId.description: (Panel only — out of scope in v1.) Highlights the active org in the panel.

onOrgSelect.description: (Panel only — out of scope in v1.) (orgId) => void when a panel row is clicked.

className.description: Additional CSS class on the root element.

accessibility.ariaLabel: Always includes the full org name (and city for Catholic orgs), regardless of visible truncation

gaps: Panel (dropdown / bottom sheet) not yet designed in Figma — trigger only ships.
ARIA pattern choice (Disclosure+listbox vs Combobox) deferred until panel is designed.
logoUrl placeholder tint (rgba(53,85,160,0.25)) is not a semantic token — TBD once brand-avatar token is added to Figma.
Panel mobile behaviour (dropdown vs bottom sheet) not yet decided.

top-nav.description: Fixed global navigation bar. Persists across all modules and viewports. Brand-blue surface, dark-mode tokens throughout. Three slots: ModuleSwitcher (left), OrgSwitcher (left), Search + ActionIcons + Profile (right). Spec status: PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.

activeModuleId.description: ID of the currently active module ('home'|'people'|'giving'|'events'|'comms')

moduleSwitcherType.description: ModuleSwitcher (app switcher) behavior. 'interactive' = chevron + hover/pressed, opens the app switcher. 'static' = Amplify Dashboard ONLY: current-module label with no chevron, no hover/pressed, not a control (nowhere to switch to from the dashboard). Maps to Figma 'Type' variant property. OrgSwitcher is unaffected.

activeOrgId.description: ID of the currently active organization

orgs.description: List of organizations the user can switch between

user.description: Current user profile for the avatar and menu

onModuleSelect.description: Called when user selects a module

onOrgSelect.description: Called when user selects an org

onSearchOpen.description: Called when search pill is clicked

onSideNavToggle.description: Called when hamburger is clicked (mobile only)

gaps: Active item token in dropdowns: uses raw #eef2fb — no semantic token exists yet (HIGH).
Notification badge / dot on bell icon not yet designed (HIGH).
Mobile profile tap behavior not specified (HIGH).
Destructive item (Sign out) uses raw red — no semantic danger token (MEDIUM).
TopNav position sticky vs fixed not resolved (MEDIUM).
Logo crop parameters tuned for Sacred Heart logo only (MEDIUM).
top-nav.moduleNote: CHANGED 2026-10-01: the bar is 60px at every breakpoint, not 56/54. top-nav.jsx already read --contextual-layout-units-topnav-height so it was correct, but top-nav.html hand-copied 56 and 54 with 4px/16px and 4px/12px padding, and nav-shell-spec.md said 56 in twelve places. The demo now reads the height, padding and gap tokens and the breakpoint classes carry no metrics at all, so there is nothing left to drift. The spec's collapsed SideNav rail also said 72px in eleven places; the real value is 84 (contextual SideNav/Width/Collapsed = Unit/84) and the repo has had it right for months.

spinner.description: Indeterminate activity indicator. 8-spoke sunburst, arbitrary size, semantic-token-only colour via tone + emphasis.
spinner.moduleNote: React module added 2026-10-01 with NewCo's RING loader alongside Amplify's sunburst, as a `variant` prop. The ring's three arcs are currentColor at three stroke opacities rather than the concept's hardcoded purples, so it answers every tone and both brand themes. spinner.html remains the standalone demo for the sunburst. SpinnerKeyframes must be mounted once per document.

label.description: Accessible name announced by screen readers

button.description: Primary action trigger. Three styles (Fill / Outlined / Naked), four semantic types (Primary / Secondary / Tertiary / Negative), four sizes (L / M / S / XS). Supports leading icon, trailing icon, icon-only, and loading states. 48×48px touch target always.

buttonStyle.description: Visual style. Fill = solid surface (highest weight). Outlined = bordered transparent. Naked = no border or fill (lowest weight).

size.description: L = 18px label, M = 16px label, S = 14px label, XS = 12px label (8/6 padding, 16px icon wrap). Touch target is always 48×48px minimum. XS is defined in Figma for Primary/Secondary/Negative only (not Tertiary).

type.description: Semantic intent. Primary = brand blue. Secondary = neutral muted. Tertiary = lightest. Negative = destructive.

text.description: Visible label text. Also used as accessible name when showText is false.

leadingIcon.description: Material Symbols ligature name (e.g. 'add', 'check'). Rendered when showLeadingIcon is true.

trailingIcon.description: Material Symbols ligature name (e.g. 'arrow_forward'). Rendered when showTrailingIcon is true.

showText.description: When false: icon-only button. ariaLabel is required when showText is false.

loading.description: Replaces content with ButtonSpinner. Sets aria-busy='true'. Implicitly disables the button.

onClick.description: Click / keyboard activation handler. Not called when disabled or loading.

ariaLabel.description: Overrides accessible name. Required when showText is false (icon-only).

className.description: Additional CSS class on the outer <button> element.

accessibility.focusRing: 6px white halo + 2px brand ring via box-shadow on Container.Main

search.description: Pill-shaped search bar (SearchInput) and top-nav wrapper (TopNavSearch). v1 covers the bar and its states (idle, hover, focused, with-value, filter-active, disabled, error) plus TopNavSearch collapsed/expanded. The Open state (results dropdown) is deferred.

filterBadge.description: Shows dot badge on filter button

nav-shell.description: Application shell — TopNav + SideNav + content area. The outermost layout wrapping every Amplify page. Compose from top-nav.jsx and sidenav.jsx — do not reimplement.

module-icon.description: The twelve Amplify module marks, in two treatments and three colour variants, on a 16x16 canvas.
module-icon.moduleNote: Size is DEPTH of colour, not of shape: Two Color resolves the module's base and subtle identity colours, One Color draws the whole mark in the base colour (Figma's own variant, not a tint), and Mono resolves every path to currentColor. The 23 --module-* identity properties are declared ON the component and resolve through PRIMITIVES rather than semantics, because a module's colour is its identity and must not flip with the theme: Giving is the same blue in Light and Midnight. This is the one place in the system where reading a primitive directly is correct. CHANGED 2026-10-01: the Figma canvas moved from 24x24 to 16x16 and the single Color value `Full` became `Two Color` plus `One Color`, so every path coordinate is re-exported rather than rescaled. `color="full"` survives as a deprecated alias for `two-color`. The default size follows the canvas and is now 16. BOTH TREATMENTS NOW HAVE ARTWORK. Figma's Style axis maps onto the prop `treatment`, not `style`, because `style` is already the CSS style object on every React component. Base is 38 paths across the twelve modules, Rippled is 66, and they are genuinely different geometry rather than a modifier. Rippled exists in Two Color and Mono only, so asking for rippled plus one-color returns Two Color rather than a flat treatment the design does not define. Equip's gradient coordinates differ by treatment, because the Rippled artwork reaches further across the frame; within a treatment all its gradients are byte-identical so one def serves them all. The three demos that carry the artwork inline (top-nav, nav-shell, module-icon) are GENERATED by scripts/sync-demo-module-icon.js, which is chained into build-dist: they used to be byte-identical 35kB hand-copies and all three silently kept drawing the 24 canvas after the module was updated.

title.note: Sets role=img and aria-label. Omit for a decorative mark beside a visible label.

module-icon.figmaNote: 60 variants: 12 modules x (Base in all three Colors + Rippled in Two Color and Mono). Both Styles are implemented and Code Connect maps the axis onto `treatment`. Home is the one module whose two treatments are identical, because its mark already fills the canvas.

skeleton.description: Loading placeholder. A block the shape of the content it replaces, with a 45 degree band sweeping bottom-left to top-right.
skeleton.moduleNote: Brought across from the NewCo and Spired design concept, token-pure. The concept hardcoded a rung of a `warm` primitive ramp that Pathway does not have, plus two literal rgba() stops; here the base is a semantic fill and the band is color-mix over tokens, so it inherits the brand theme and inverts in Midnight. SkeletonKeyframes must be mounted once per document: a module that injects CSS on import cannot be tree-shaken.
skeleton.specNote: No spec yet. Transcribed from the design concept rather than from a Figma component; there is no Figma node for it.
skeleton.figmaNote: No Figma component. The design lives in the NewCo and Spired concept, not in the Figma library.

circle.note: squares the box and fully rounds it, for avatars

lastLineWidth.note: short on purpose: equal-length bars read as a table, not prose

widget.description: The resizable dashboard building block. A header carrying the title, refresh and resize, plus a content slot. Size is depth: Glance, Explore, Detail, Full.
widget.moduleNote: Size is depth, not scale: resizing changes what the content shows. Flat at Glance (one surface, no content toolbar) and layered everywhere else, driven by the presence of content controls rather than by size directly. A KPI tile is not a separate component: it is Widget at Glance holding a Metric. Hover-revealed info and go-to icons are suppressed at Glance because their 36px targets hold layout even at opacity 0 and would eat most of a 130px title. WidgetKeyframes must be mounted once per document and also declares the --pw-widget-cols-* spans, so the breakpoint lives in a media query rather than a JS branch.
widget.specNote: The authoritative spec is widget-container-spec.md in the working folder, not in this repo. Its sections 3.1, 4 and 8.3 predate the token families that now exist (warm surfaces, radius, spacing, motion, elevation, touch targets) and describe them as raw values; the implementation binds all of them. Its section 5.1 names four sizes Small/Wide/Tall/Large, which section 0 supersedes with Glance/Explore/Detail/Full.
widget.demoNote: Shares the dashboard demo, because a widget on its own cannot show the grid, the manage mode or the resize flow.
widget.figmaNote: The component set carries three Size variants (Glance, Detail, Explore). Full is a separate Widget.Focus FRAME (40010500:6815), not a variant, so no Figma instance can emit size="full"; a consumer picks it explicitly. The NewCo section is a mirror and is read-only.
widget.tokenNote: Widget/MinWidth/{Glance,Detail,Explore} added to Contextual: Layout & Units 2026-10-02 on request. Values from Figma Widget 40009622:39702, which carries a minWidth per variant: 275 / 515 / 1050. Full has no entry: it spans every track so its floor is the grid's.

dashboard.description: The dashboard page template: the toolbar, the widget grid, and the templated flow for managing a dashboard and adding widgets.
dashboard.moduleNote: Owns the grid (4/8/12 columns by breakpoint, 48px row unit, dense row flow so widgets pull up and leftover space collects at the bottom) and the two modes. The save matrix is the part that is easy to get wrong: editing the System dashboard always names and creates a NEW custom dashboard, so the shipped baseline is never overwritten, while editing a custom dashboard saves back to it. There is no drag-to-pixel-position and no drag-to-resize; size is picked from the widget's own menu and compaction is always on.
dashboard.specNote: dashboard-shell-spec.md in the working folder, still marked DRAFT. Its four open questions are unresolved: the meaning of 'Reset to default' (implemented here as 'Discard changes', which is reading (a) only), whether a first save of an edited System dashboard should also offer to make it the default, what the real view-mode widget actions are besides Refresh, and what the unsaved-changes guard should do when switching dashboards (implemented here as: the switcher simply does not act while there are unsaved changes).
dashboard.figmaNote: The organism page is 'Dashboards'. The add-widget and manage flows live on the templated-flow page 'Dashboards: Add Widgets, Edit Dashboards', section 'Add Widget & Manage Flows v2'.
dashboard.codeConnectNote: NOT code connected, and cannot be. The 'Dashboards' organism page is screen frames and the templated-flow page is spec panels and annotated deep-dives; neither contains a COMPONENT or COMPONENT_SET, so there is no node to map. Code Connect binds code to a component, not to a screen. If the dashboard shell is ever built as a Figma component, map it then.

page-template.description: The screen template every Amplify page is built on: the top-navigation region, the page-navigation region, and a responsive sheet holding the page heading, tabs, toolbar and sections.
page-template.moduleNote: Owns the regions, the sheet and the four page-level compositions that only ever appear inside a page (PageHeading, PageTabs, PageToolbar, PageSection). It does NOT own what goes in the slots: TopNav and SideNav are passed in, and Card, Input, FilterChip, Heading, Button and the Tabs atoms are separate library components that do not exist in this repo yet. The sheet is the one responsive piece: its padding and corner radius resolve through Responsive: Layout by media query, so there is no JS branch for them.
page-template.specNote: No spec in this repo. The Figma component set is the source.
page-template.demoNote: No standalone demo: the Storybook stories compose it with the real TopNav, SideNav and Widget, which a self-contained CDN page cannot do without duplicating all three.
page-template.figmaNote: The component set is called ScreenTemplate, not Page Template; Page Template is the page it sits on. Its third breakpoint variant value is literally 'Breakpoint3', not 'Mobile', and the Code Connect enum has to match that verbatim or the prop comes back undefined for every mobile instance. Worth renaming in Figma.
page-template.tokenGap: RESOLVED 2026-10-02 and it was not what I first reported. The six Contextual/Page*, Contextual/Section/* and Contextual/ToolBar/* gap variables were not library-resolved at all: they were DELETED variables. A deleted variable still resolves by id, so the bindings rendered, but it is absent from the local list and from the export, so the Page Template was bound to six dangling references that could never be exported, synced or maintained. They aliased Unit/8 and Unit/16 directly, reaching past the semantic layer into primitives. All 48 affected bindings in the ScreenTemplate set were rebound onto the live semantic tokens of the SAME value, Gap/Tight (8) x26 and Gap/Base (16) x22, guarded so a value change would have rolled the whole call back. No new tokens were created. ScreenTemplate's own nodes now carry zero dangling bindings.
page-template.figmaOpen: Still outstanding, and all of it belongs to NESTED components rather than to ScreenTemplate: 87 bindings still point at deleted variables (FilterChip 84 across three deleted ids, Input 3), and 53 bindings use the primitive Unit/10 directly for spacing (Card 20, FilterChip 12, Heading 9, PW_Button 6, Page Heading 3, Heading.Style 3). Unit/10 has NO semantic equivalent: the Gap scale is 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36, so mapping it means moving the value to 8 or 12, which is a design decision rather than a mapping and is Jo's call.

card.description: A surface holding a heading, a subtitle, a body and a supporting-content slot, optionally with a leading icon, and optionally a target.
card.moduleNote: Figma gives Card five States, which only make sense if the whole surface is a target, so onClick decides: with it the card renders as a button and carries hover, active and focus; without it the card is a plain div and those states are unreachable. A card that looks pressable and is not is worse than either. Figma's four content toggles (ShowHeading, Show CardSubtitle, ShowCardBody, ShowIconLeading, ShowCardSupportingContent) collapse into the presence of the content props themselves, because a boolean that only means "is the next prop set" is a Figma limitation rather than an API. States are distinguished by border width AND colour plus shadow depth, never by colour alone, and nothing translates on hover.
card.specNote: No spec in this repo. The Figma component set is the source.
card.demoNote: No standalone demo: the Storybook stories cover the state matrix, the container-versus-target distinction and the content combinations, which is everything the component does.
card.figmaNote: Four identical Card sets exist across the page, two per brand section, so the section is the only thing that tells them apart. This maps the Amplify one.
card.tokenGap: RESOLVED 2026-10-02: no new tokens needed. Figma binds Elevation/Card/Rest, /Hover and /Pressed, which are not in the panel's Elevation collection (it holds Lift, Overlay, Sheet and Widget), but their COMPONENTS are all semantic and present: shadow-card-rest|hover|pressed x/y/blur/spread plus fill-shadow-dropshadow. The component composes the shadows from those exactly as the Figma effect does, so it is already semantic-only and no contextual card elevation tokens are required.

heading.description: A heading. `level` picks the tag, `context`/`size`/`weight` pick the appearance, and the two are independent.
heading.moduleNote: Figma has TWO orthogonal sets and this keeps them orthogonal. `Heading` (40004143:1824) carries Level H1 to H6 and all six render identically at 24/30 Bold, so Level is the semantic level and nothing more; `Heading.Style` (40004024:31157) carries the appearance. A page's h1 can be Section/Small if the layout wants that, and a visually huge heading can be an h2. Only 27 of the 72 Context x Size x Weight combinations exist, and they are listed EXPLICITLY rather than derived as a cross product, because the grid is sparse in both directions: Section defines XSmall in Medium and Semibold but not Bold, and XXS in Medium only, while Local defines Base in Bold and Semibold but Small in Semibold only. A cross product gives 31, four of which Figma does not draw. An undrawn size falls back to the nearest defined one in its context, and an undrawn weight falls back to one that context and size actually define. Figma's heading styles are TEXT STYLES, not variables, so they do not export and there is no composite token to bind; every value is composed from the panel's type pieces. Section/Base is 18/30, which is line-height-m-RELAXED rather than the single 24, and that is a real pairing because a section heading sits over body copy.
heading.demoNote: No standalone demo: the stories render every one of the 27 defined combinations, which is the whole component.
heading.figmaNote: Heading.Style is the appearance set and is what Code Connect maps. The Level set is deliberately unmapped: a snippet from it could only say level={n} with no style, which is less useful than nothing.
heading.figmaDefect: Three Heading.Style variants have their Weight label inverted against what they render: Section/XSmall/Weight=Medium renders SemiBold, Section/XSmall/Weight=Semibold renders Medium, and Section/XXS/Weight=Medium renders SemiBold. The component honours the LABEL, because weight="medium" has to give 500, so those three render differently here than in Figma until the file is corrected. Needs a fix in Figma, not in code.

badge.description: A status pill. Eight statuses, three sizes, four styles, with optional leading and trailing icons.
badge.moduleNote: Three of the four Figma styles are systematic: outline-fill, fill and outline each read the same three tokens per status (fill, stroke, foreground) and differ only in which of the three they apply, so STATUS is the whole colour story and `style` is a switch. The border is always declared and goes transparent when a style has none, so a badge does not change size between styles. Accent 2 is Jade and Accent 3 is Mauve, which is what those variants bind, and the props are named for the colour rather than the number because a number that only means "the next accent we added" tells a consumer nothing. There is no Accent 1: Info already resolves to the Amethyst ramp. Three statuses do not follow the obvious token pattern and the table records what they actually bind: Neutral uses the neutral BOLD stroke and foreground rather than an on-subtle, Attention uses the STRONG stroke rather than subtle, and the two accents use an unsuffixed stroke because that is the only one those families have. The prop is `badgeStyle`, not `style`, because `style` is the CSS style object.
badge.demoNote: No standalone demo: the stories cover all 96 combinations plus the Naked divergence side by side.
badge.figmaNote: The page carries FOUR older 63-variant Badge sets that still report variant conflicts, alongside the clean 96-variant sets, two per brand. The node id is the only thing that picks the right one; this maps the clean Amplify set.
badge.figmaDefect: Style=Naked, re-read 2026-10-02 after a pass on the file. MUCH BETTER, NOT YET FIXED. Progress: the raw primitive is gone (Accent 3 no longer binds Mauve/25) and there are no non-semantic fills left anywhere; Accent 2 and Accent 3 are now fully consistent and genuinely bare across all three sizes; most statuses now carry their own on-subtle foreground rather than the neutral one; Small is almost entirely correct. Outstanding: five statuses still carry a FILL in at least one size (Neutral/Large, Severe/Large, Negative/Large+Medium, Attention/Large+Medium, Info/Large+Medium) and five still carry a BORDER (Neutral all three, Severe/Large+Medium, Negative/Large, Positive/Large+Medium, Attention/Large), so only two of the eight are consistent across their own sizes. NEW DEFECT, and the priority: Positive/Small binds foreground-static-SEVERE-on-subtle, so a positive badge renders in severe's colour. That is a wrong-status foreground rather than a loudness problem. The component continues to render no fill, no border and the status foreground for all eight, which is what Accent 2 and Accent 3 now do and what Small nearly does, so the file is converging on it.
badge.figmaOpen: Re-read the CANONICAL set 40011003:15892 on 2026-10-02 after the owner's pass. 464 of 473 paints carry a PAINT STYLE with the correct Pathway name; 0 carry a variable; 9 carry neither. All 9 are FILLS on Style=Outline variants, which by definition should have none: Neutral/Small plus Large for Neutral, Severe, Attention, Negative, Positive, Info, Accent 2 and Accent 3. They want removing rather than tokenising, so the repo has not consumed them. NOTE for any future reader: a reader that checks only boundVariables reports this set as 100 percent raw hex, which is wrong.

radio.description: A radio option and the group it belongs in. Checked and error are booleans; state is derived from interaction.
radio.moduleNote: RadioGroup ships WITH Radio, because a radio is never alone: a lone radio cannot be unselected by the user, has no arrow-key behaviour, and has nothing for its label to describe. The group owns the name, the value, roving tabindex (one tab stop for the whole group, skipping disabled options) and arrow-key navigation. Figma's State axis is a drawing convenience and is NOT a prop: hover, focus and pressed are things the browser already knows, so they are derived, and forceState exists for the Storybook matrix only. Figma's four-value Type axis collapses into two booleans, checked and error, because Selected and Error Selected are the same selection in different validity. Geometry from the variants: ring 20 at Base and 22 at Large, dot 10 shown only when checked, hover halo 42 painted only on hover and focus, hit area 44 which is the AA touch target. The halo is what makes a 20px ring meet a 44px target without the ring growing.
radio.demoNote: No standalone demo: the stories cover all 20 Base combinations, both sizes, the disabled label, and a live keyboard-navigable group.
radio.figmaNote: 25 variants, not 40: the Base size is complete at 20, and Large has only 5. See figmaDefect.
radio.figmaDefect: TWO defects. (1) Size=Large exists for Unselected ONLY, five variants of a possible twenty. CONFIRMED 2026-10-02 as unfinished Figma rather than intent: Selected and Error should get a Large, which is what the component already renders, scaling the ring from 20 to 22 and leaving the dot, halo and hit area as drawn. Needs finishing in Figma. (2) The label never dims when disabled: all twenty variants bind foreground-static-neutral-base including the Disabled ones. The component dims it to foreground-action-disabled, because a disabled control whose label looks enabled reads as a bug.

top-nav-actions.description: The action icons that sit at the right-hand end of the TopNav bar.
top-nav-actions.moduleNote: Belongs to the nav-shell family rather than to TopNav: top-nav.figma.ts maps the BAR only, and the panels and icons that open out of it are separate patterns. Has no story and no Code Connect yet.

alert.description: An inline message: heading, body, optional icon, optional action, optional dismiss. Six types.
alert.moduleNote: FIGMA'S TYPE NAMES AND THE TOKEN FAMILIES THEY RESOLVE TO DISAGREE, and the props keep Figma's names so a designer and a developer are talking about the same thing: Success is positive, Alert is severe, Warning is attention, Error is negative, Tertiary is info, Neutral is neutral. `Alert` as a Type inside a component called Alert means the severe level, not "an alert". TYPE_FAMILY records the real mapping. Role is chosen by type rather than passed: error and alert get role=alert with aria-live assertive, the other four get role=status with polite, because a screen reader should not be made to announce a success message over whatever the user is doing. That is an accessibility decision, not a design one, so Code Connect does not emit it. The heading icon has no bound fill in Figma, so it and the dismiss control both inherit currentColor and neither is a second colour decision per type. The text ban does not apply to this component: an Alert's job IS a sentence, so heading and body are content rather than explanation.
alert.demoNote: No standalone demo: the stories cover all six types, the content combinations, live dismissal and the Tertiary border gap side by side.
alert.figmaNote: Four identical Alert sets exist on the page, so the node id is the only thing that picks the right one. This maps the Amplify one.

scroll-to-enable.description: A block of content the user must reach the end of before the checkbox beneath it can be ticked.
scroll-to-enable.moduleNote: Lives in components/checkbox/ rather than its own folder because it is not a new control: it is the Checkbox plus a precondition, and it composes the real Checkbox rather than restyling one. FOUR DECISIONS MAKE OR BREAK IT. (1) Once the end is reached the checkbox STAYS enabled; re-locking would punish a user who scrolls up to re-read a clause and would let the control flicker as the page moves. (2) The scroll region is KEYBOARD OPERABLE, tabIndex 0 on a real overflow container, so arrow keys, Page Down and End all reach the end. Without that a keyboard-only or switch user could never satisfy the precondition and could never submit, which turns a gate into a hard block; this is the part implementations usually miss. (3) Content SHORTER than its box counts as read, because a box with no bottom to reach would otherwise lock the form forever on a tall screen. (4) It RE-MEASURES via ResizeObserver, because a font loading, a window resize or late content all change whether the end has been reached, and measuring once on mount is how this breaks in production. The bottom fade is decorative and aria-hidden: the hint line carries the same information as text, so the fade is never the only cue. The readiness change is announced through a polite live region. The locked hint is the only prose the component renders and it earns its place: a disabled checkbox with no stated reason looks broken.
scroll-to-enable.demoNote: No standalone demo: the stories cover the keyboard path, the short-content case and the error state, which is everything the pattern decides.
scroll-to-enable.figmaNote: The Figma page is DOCUMENTATION and screenshots: it contains no COMPONENT or COMPONENT_SET, so there was nothing to transcribe variant by variant. The behaviour comes from the pattern and from the Checkbox it wraps, and the page is a reference rather than a source. If it is ever built as a component, map it then.
